summary: Comments from UCLA-NMC on the draft Data Transfer Protocol and File Transfer Protocol after trying to implement them. They point out an ambiguity in the length of the sequence number field and suggest simplifying the transaction header, and raise other problems the implementation revealed.

eli5.summary: People tried building the file-sending rules and found places that were unclear, so they suggest fixes.

subtitle: Implementation feedback on the proposed Data and File Transfer Protocols

tldr.problem: The draft Data Transfer Protocol and File Transfer Protocol have ambiguities and design choices that make them difficult to implement.
tldr.mechanism: UCLA-NMC shares implementation experience, pointing out a 16-bit vs. 8-bit discrepancy in sequence number fields and raising the complexities of the Append transaction.
tldr.outcome: Clarification and revision of these ambiguities would accelerate the implementation schedule and improve protocol utility.

today: This feedback RFC is historical, documenting early implementation experience with protocols that evolved into modern file transfer systems.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: RFC 250 offers feedback from UCLA-NMC on the proposed Data Transfer Protocol (RFC 171) and File Transfer Protocol (RFC 172). As interest in moving larger amounts of data than typical TELNET transfers grows, implementation attempts have revealed several difficulties with the proposed designs.
sections.eli5: People at UCLA tried to build the file-sending system and found problems with the design.

sections.title: The Sequence Number Field Problem
sections.content: RFC 171 specifies a 16-bit sequence number field in the descriptor and count transaction header, but uses an 8-bit field in the error codes transaction. This inconsistency is confusing. UCLA-NMC believes 8 bits is sufficient for a sequence number and proposes reducing it to 8 bits. Removing the two null bytes from the descriptor header would also shrink its total size from 72 bits to 48 bits, matching the size of a typical 50-bit transaction header and making implementation more convenient.
sections.eli5: One part of the message uses a 16-bit counter but another part uses 8 bits. Making them match would make the code simpler.

sections.title: The Append Transaction Ambiguity
sections.content: Implementation in time-sharing systems like SEX reveals that determining the end of a file is almost entirely context-dependent: the program reading the file decides when it reaches the end. This makes the meaning of an Append transaction hazy. Since the proposed Mail Box Protocol relies on the Append feature, not properly defining this command significantly reduces the file transfer service's usefulness.
sections.eli5: Different programs decide when a file ends in different ways. The Append command doesn't explain what that means clearly enough.

sections.title: Path Forward
sections.content: Resolving these ambiguities would greatly accelerate the implementation schedule, at least at UCLA-NMC, and would lead to better protocol definitions that work across different types of computer systems.
sections.eli5: Clearing up these issues would help teams build the system faster and better.

references.text: Crocker, S. D., "Proposed Revision of the ARPANET Data Transfer Protocol", RFC 171.
Postel, J. B., "A Proposed Service for Public Access to ARPA Network Data", RFC 172.
